affiliations.research_notes: The obituary explicitly places brief civilian War Department employment before active Army duty and later OSS service. Army service intervened, so this is not labeled immediate pre-OSS affiliation.
The institutional biography says Shrady's established artistic career was placed on hold when he enlisted in June 1943. The Army preceded his brief OSS assignment.

A 1939 VMI register transcription lists William Gerhard Suhling Jr. as company president. Official Army history supplies the Lt. Col. Suhling OSS bridge, but neither source proves the company was his immediate pre-OSS affiliation.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Myron Shpur is a confirmed match to the official Army record and the Washington Post obituary describing his Army and OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact name, nonshared protected identifier, and obituary's Army-to-OSS chronology agree.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the exact official Army match and an independent obituary explicitly naming Army and OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The obituary distinguishes civilian War Department work, active Army duty, OSS service, and later CIA employment.
claims.match_notes: Army-coded occupation data are not used as employer evidence.

claims.claim_text: Myron Shpur worked briefly as a civilian for the U.S. War Department before beginning active Army duty.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The obituary explicitly places War Department civilian employment immediately before active Army duty and later OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact name, official Army identity evidence, and the obituary's OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the last civilian affiliation before Army service; Army duty intervened before OSS service.
claims.match_notes: This is not labeled immediate pre-OSS because the source explicitly places Army service between the civilian job and OSS.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Frederick C Shrady is a confirmed match to the artist and Army officer documented by the Monuments Men and Women Foundation.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full name and nonshared protected identifier agree, and the institutional biography explicitly documents a brief OSS assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact official Army data and an independent institutional biography linking the same full name to OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The biography provides a coherent prewar artist, June 1943 Army enlistment, and brief OSS chronology.
claims.match_notes: Frederick Charles Shrady is retained as a documented full-name variant.

claims.claim_text: Frederick C. Shrady was a self-employed artist before his June 1943 Army enlistment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional biography describes an established full-time painting career that was placed on hold upon enlistment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact Army identity evidence and the biography's explicit OSS bridge.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the civilian occupation immediately preceding enlistment; the Army preceded the brief OSS assignment.
claims.match_notes: No employing organization is invented; the relationship is modeled as self-employment.

claims.claim_text: The Box 708 Kenneth D Shuckers row shares a protected identifier with a separate Box 688 Kenneth D Schuckers row, creating an unresolved duplicate conflict.

claims.claim_text: The indexed W G Shuling is a high-confidence spelling variant of Lt. Col. William G. Suhling Jr., an OSS and Strategic Services Unit officer in Germany.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon initials, near-identical surname, lieutenant-colonel rank, and direct OSS mission context align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare near-match, exact initials, compatible rank, and official Army history's direct OSS identification.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army history documents Suhling in the OSS-to-SSU transition in Germany during 1945-1946.
claims.match_notes: The printed index spelling Shuling remains preserved; Suhling is added as a documented variant rather than silently replacing it.

claims.claim_text: A 1939 VMI register lists William Gerhard Suhling Jr. as president of Suhling & Company, Inc., a Lynchburg leaf-tobacco business.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The contemporary institutional register identifies Suhling and his corporate role; a 1940 federal publication independently confirms the company.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the full-name register entry plus the official Army history's matching initials, rank, and OSS role.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented in 1939, before OSS, but not shown to be the immediate predecessor to military or OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The role is visibly qualified because the accessible register text is a third-party transcription and the index surname differs by one letter.
